title: Q: Determine the weight of oxide formed by heating 1 g of a carbonate (using the law of definite proportions)
notes: **Data:** 0.36 g of a metal burnt in oxygen yields 0.60 g of oxide; the carbonate of that metal contains 28.57% of the metal
From the oxide experiment: mass of metal = 0.36 g, mass of oxide = 0.60 g → ratio (mass of metal)/(mass of oxide) = 0.36/0.60 = **0.6**
From the carbonate experiment: 1 g of carbonate contains 28.57% metal → mass of metal in 1 g carbonate = 0.2857 g
By the Law of Definite Proportions, the metal-to-oxide ratio stays fixed at 0.6, so: 0.2857 / (mass of oxide) = 0.6
